punchline: Darwin's working day added up to about four hours; the rest was sofa, walks, newspaper and backgammon.
thirty_sec: Pang looks at Darwin's day. After eight he worked about ninety minutes, rested an hour on the sofa while his wife Emma read to him, then worked about ninety minutes more. Midday brought a walk on the gravel Sandwalk behind his garden, and an hour of work in the late afternoon. The total came to about four hours. Pang reads the breaks as deliberate rest, though critics say one routine does not prove four hours suits everyone.
